source: Gentoo Portage profile masks plus curated new-user explanations

no_mask: No package.mask entry in the downloaded database matched this package.
If emerge still calls it masked, check the exact emerge message: it may be a keyword mask, a mask in your local /etc/portage, or a mask added after this database was built.
meaning: Portage is refusing this package on purpose. That is different from a download failure.
steps: 1. Read the mask reason before changing anything.
2. Put the exact atom in /etc/portage/package.unmask if it is hard-masked.
3. Put the exact atom in /etc/portage/package.accept_keywords if emerge says the keyword is missing.
4. Re-run the emerge command and read the next message.
messages.built: Local Portage entries merged; database now has {count} entries at {path}.
messages.missing: No database at {path}. Run: gentoo explain db fetch
messages.guide_missing: No explanation named {name}. Run: gentoo explain guides
messages.lookup_none: No guide or mask entry matched {query}. Try: gentoo explain guides

tips.title: Hard mask vs keyword mask:
tips.body:
A hard mask lives in package.mask and means the distro or your config says no.
  A keyword mask means the package is not marked stable for your architecture.
  They need different fixes, so read the emerge message carefully.

tips.title: Use exact atoms:
tips.body:
Prefer =category/package-version over a bare package name when unmasking.
  That limits the change to one version and makes later undo easy.

tips.title: Before unmasking:
tips.body: Read the mask comment, check USE flags with emerge --verbose, and remember that masks often exist for broken builds or security reasons.

tips.title: Downloaded DB vs local DB:
tips.body: The downloaded database covers Gentoo profile masks. Run `gentoo explain db build` to merge your own /etc/portage entries into the local copy.

tips.title: Offline use:
tips.body: Run `gentoo explain db fetch` once while online. After that every `gentoo explain masked <package>` lookup reads only the local compressed database.

tips.title: Read the whole emerge error:
tips.body: The last line is often only a summary. The useful line is usually the first ERROR or the blocked package list above it.

tips.title: Dry run before changing config:
tips.body:
Use --ask so Portage shows the plan before it changes the system.
  Example: emerge --ask --verbose <package>

tips.title: One change at a time:
tips.body:
Change one mask, keyword, or USE flag, then rerun emerge.
  That makes it obvious which edit fixed or broke things.

tips.title: Keep a config backup:
tips.body:
Copy /etc/portage before a bigger change.
  Example: sudo cp -a /etc/portage /etc/portage.backup

tips.title: Use exact package atoms:
tips.body:
=category/package-version limits the change to one version.
  category/package applies to the whole package and is broader.

tips.title: Mask reason first:
tips.body:
The comment above a mask usually gives a removal date or bug number.
  Read it before overriding the mask.

tips.title: Short forms:
tips.body:
gentoo <package> checks a masked package.
  gentoo <guide> opens a guide.
  gentoo with no arguments lists guides.

guides.title: Why a package is masked
body: A mask is Portage refusing a package on purpose.
It is different from a missing download or a compile error.
package.mask: a hard mask; the distro or your config says no.
keyword: the version is not marked stable for your architecture.
license: the license is not accepted in your config.
Only override a mask after reading the comment above it.

guides.title: Stable vs testing keywords
body: Portage keywords say how mature a version is for your architecture.
Use the exact atom from the emerge error instead of a broad rule.

guides.title: Unmasking safely
body: Unmasking is not the same as accepting a keyword.
Hard masks live in package.mask; keyword problems live in acceptance files.
Then rerun emerge and read the next message.

guides.title: USE flags
body: USE flags choose optional features when a package is built.
See current flags for a package:
After changing USE flags, update affected packages:

guides.title: Blocked packages
body: A blocker means two packages or slots cannot be installed together.
Remove or unmerge the conflicting package.
Change a USE flag that pulled in the conflict.
Install a different slot if both versions are needed.
Read each suggested change before accepting it.

guides.title: Slots
body: A slot lets more than one version of a package stay installed.
The part after a colon is the slot, such as dev-libs/foo:0 or dev-libs/foo:1.
If versions conflict, check whether the target package needs a specific slot.
Do not mask a whole package when only one slot is the problem.

guides.title: License masks
body: Gentoo can refuse a package because its license is not accepted.
Read the emerge error for the exact license name.
Accept one license for one package:
Accept a license globally only when you understand what it means.

guides.title: Keeping Gentoo updated
body: Large updates are easier to debug when you do them often.

guides.title: gentoo explain database
body: It ships as db.json.gz and db.json.
Download or refresh the compressed database:
Merge your own /etc/portage entries after fetching:
After one fetch, lookups work offline.

guides.title: Easy ways to run gentoo explain
body: gentoo <package>  explain why that package is masked
gentoo fetch  refresh the downloaded database
gentoo path  show the local database path
Run one fetch while online, then everything works offline.
